initial_plan.can_answer: partly: describes the annual number of Brooklyn crash records with at least one reported pedestrian injury or death, but not an exposure-adjusted safety risk or the cause of any change
initial_plan.metric: Annual count of crash rows with number_of_pedestrians_injured > 0 or number_of_pedestrians_killed > 0, counting each crash once
initial_plan.denominator: None; an annual crash-record count, not a rate
initial_plan.population: Police-reported crash rows with borough Brooklyn and a non-null crash_date in 2013 or later; a crash is counted once if it reports at least one pedestrian injured or killed
initial_plan.years: Every calendar year from 2013 through the latest year represented by the file, subject to file coverage
initial_plan.data_check: Pending; inspect row coverage and missingness in the two injury/death columns used to identify pedestrian-injury crashes before deciding how to treat unknown outcomes.

data_check_interpretation.facts: The initial case-sensitive borough comparison returned no matching rows; normalizing borough with lower(trim()) produced 483,501 Brooklyn crash rows for 2013-2026. Among those rows, 0 had a missing/unknown borough or missing crash_date, and 0 had a null or negative value in either pedestrian injury/death field. Each full year from 2013 through 2025 had date coverage from January 1 through December 31; 2026 had 9,700 rows from January 1 through June 11 and is partial. Included full-year row counts range from 47,024 in 2013 and a peak of 50,851 in 2015 to 22,785 in 2024 and 24,303 in 2025.
data_check_interpretation.decisions: Changed the borough filter to case- and whitespace-normalized Brooklyn because the literal initial filter matched no rows. Keep all eligible 2013-2025 rows and classify them using the two pedestrian outcome fields; neither field is missing or impossible in the check population, so no crash has unknown pedestrian-involvement status from these fields. Exclude all 2026 rows (9,700) from the plotted trend because the file only covers that year through June 11; this changes the initial through-latest-year range to complete calendar years only.

final_plan.can_answer: partly: describes the annual share of Brooklyn police-reported crash records that include a reported pedestrian injury or death, but not a pedestrian-exposure-adjusted safety risk or its cause
final_plan.metric: For each calendar year, count each selected crash row once if number_of_pedestrians_injured > 0 or number_of_pedestrians_killed > 0, then divide by all selected Brooklyn crash rows in that year and report as a percentage
final_plan.denominator: All police-reported Brooklyn crash rows with valid crash_date in that calendar year; each row is one crash record, not a pedestrian or travel-exposure unit
final_plan.population: All police-reported crash rows with lower(trim(borough)) = 'brooklyn' and crash_date in calendar years 2013-2025, inclusive; only complete calendar years are included
final_plan.years: 2013-2025 inclusive; the partial 2026 year is excluded
final_plan.limitations: This measures the fraction of crash reports with a pedestrian casualty, not the risk per pedestrian, trip, or distance walked. Checks found 0 missing or negative values in either classification field among the 2013-2026 Brooklyn check population; 2026 was only covered through June 11 (9,700 rows), so it is excluded. The crash-record denominator ranges from 50,851 in 2015 to 22,785 in 2024, so the percentage describes composition in a changing crash-record pool rather than a constant exposure base.
